# What the network guard calls local. Read by BOTH predicates' tests: the
# Python one of the wrapper (src/tool/wrapper.rs, `is_local`) and the Rust one
# (src/netguard.rs, `is_local`), so that the two cannot drift apart.
#
# One line per range, both edges where an edge means something:
#   <address> <local|public>   # what the line is for
# An address the Rust parser does not read (`IpAddr::from_str`) must be
# `local`: the Python predicate refuses what it cannot parse, and the Rust
# test checks that every such line is one no URL host could be.

# 0.0.0.0/8 ("this network")
0.0.0.0 local
0.255.255.255 local
1.0.0.0 public
# 10/8
9.255.255.255 public
10.0.0.0 local
10.255.255.255 local
11.0.0.0 public
# 100.64/10 (CGNAT: Python's is_private does not cover it)
100.63.255.255 public
100.64.0.0 local
100.127.255.255 local
100.128.0.0 public
# 127/8
126.255.255.255 public
127.0.0.0 local
127.0.0.1 local
127.255.255.255 local
128.0.0.0 public
# 169.254/16 (link-local)
169.253.255.255 public
169.254.0.0 local
169.254.255.255 local
169.255.0.0 public
# 172.16/12
172.15.255.255 public
172.16.0.0 local
172.31.255.255 local
172.32.0.0 public
# 192.168/16
192.167.255.255 public
192.168.0.0 local
192.168.255.255 local
192.169.0.0 public
# 224/4 multicast, then 240/4 reserved (the broadcast address with it)
223.255.255.255 public
224.0.0.0 local
239.255.255.255 local
240.0.0.0 local
255.255.255.255 local
# Public IPv4
8.8.8.8 public
1.1.1.1 public

# ::/96: unspecified, loopback, and the deprecated IPv4-compatible form
:: local
::1 local
::ffff:ffff local
::1:0:0 public
# fc00::/7 (unique local)
fbff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff public
fc00:: local
fdff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff local
fe00:: public
# fe80::/10 (link-local), then fec0::/10 (site-local, deprecated)
fe7f:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff public
fe80:: local
febf:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff local
fec0:: local
feff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff local
# ff00::/8 (multicast)
ff00:: local
ff02::1 local
ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff local
# Public IPv6
2001:4860:4860::8888 public
2606:4700::1111 public

# ::ffff:0:0/96 (IPv4-mapped): judged on the IPv4
::ffff:192.168.1.1 local
::ffff:127.0.0.1 local
::ffff:100.64.0.1 local
::ffff:8.8.8.8 public
# 64:ff9b::/96 (NAT64): judged on the embedded IPv4
64:ff9b::c0a8:101 local
64:ff9b::7f00:1 local
64:ff9b::808:808 public
64:ff9b::1:0:0 public
# 64:ff9b:1::/48 (local-use NAT64, RFC 8215): where the IPv4 sits depends on
# the operator's prefix length, so the whole block is refused
64:ff9b:1:: local
64:ff9b:1:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff local
64:ff9b:2:: public
# 2002::/16 (6to4): judged on the IPv4 in bits 16-47
2002:c0a8:101:: local
2002:7f00:1:: local
2002:a00:1:: local
2002:808:808:: public
2001:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff public
2003:: public

# Unparseable: refused
not-an-ip local
2130706433 local
127.1 local
192.168.1 local
::ffff:999.1.1.1 local
fe80::1%eth0 local
